clue.text: Paint extremities of docile ancient Highlander

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters, so only the ends of docile are used

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to paint the outer reaches of a meek ancient Scottish warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint a scene is to portray or represent it in pictures, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Month is busy (except the first) in a settling way

parts.note: DEC is the standard abbreviation for December
taken as written

indicators.note: the word for busy loses its opening letter, as the clue excludes the first

parts.note: a busy place is lively

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a month has been hectic, apart from its opening days.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive blow settles a matter, so acting in a way that settles things is acting conclusively.

clue.text: Going the other way, presumably down stage

indicators.note: going the other way means the letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: something down is presumably not up

explanation.surface: An actor heads away from the audience, which in theatre talk would be called downstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' is a verb here: to stage a play is to mount it. Downstage is toward the audience, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a production of a play in the theatre is to present or perform it, an idiom.

clue.text: House excessively in prison

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the word for prison, as in signals containment

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessively

explanation.surface: Someone is shut away in jail far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) is British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small country dwelling, a kind of home.

clue.text: Romantic writer to make earth move in crude transport?

parts.note: a cart is a simple, rough vehicle
earth in the sense of ground or soil is land

explanation.surface: A romantic novelist sets out to shift soil using a primitive wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'cart land': to make earth move in a crude vehicle. Barbara Cartland was a prolific English writer of romantic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Cartland wrote hundreds of romance novels, so she is an example of a writer of romantic fiction.

clue.text: Military leader at the office once more

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
someone at the office is in, present at work

explanation.surface: The general is back at his desk again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more is doing it a second time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A drop from a bar may occupy this gymnast

definitions.text: A drop from a bar may occupy this
definitions.meaning: a drink served at a bar may be poured into a glass of this type
an acrobat who does somersaults and flips

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a straight-sided drinking glass and an acrobat who performs somersaults.

clue.text: Ticket holders expect this guilty revelation

definitions.meaning: people with tickets expect entry to the venue

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both entry to a place and a confession of guilt.

clue.text: Workplace details employees should know up front

indicators.note: the letters at the front of each word are taken, read up the down entry

explanation.surface: Staff are told the essential details of their place of work at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk is the piece of furniture where an office worker does their job, so it stands for a workplace.

clue.text: Whole of eternity in torment?

indicators.note: something in torment is twisted and racked, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Suffering forever, as in a vision of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something is all of it, its complete extent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: No farewell returned among spies being unresponsive

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed among the letters for spies, so it goes inside

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of spies

indicators.note: returned means the pieces for no and farewell are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ta-ta is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: Agents refuse to say goodbye and sit there without reacting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is a casual British goodbye; 'returned' turns it and 'No' around before they go among the spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a state of stupor in which a person does not react to stimulation, an unresponsive condition.

clue.text: Complaint in letter from Greek politicians

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Greek politicians write a letter of grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' means an illness here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a viral disease, and complaint can mean an ailment or illness.

clue.text: Man's liaison set out in tabloid feature?

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped and the S is kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A man's affair is splashed across a scandal sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid exaggeration to excite readers is characteristic of the tabloid press, so it is an example of what tabloids feature.

clue.text: Essential to involve company for rambling

indicators.note: to involve means to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an essential quality is inherent, built in

explanation.surface: It is vital to bring a firm into the discussion when it wanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling speech wanders without logical connection, so it is disjointed and hard to follow.

clue.text: Border such as minister pushed back

indicators.note: pushed back means both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: eg stands for exempli gratia, for example
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman is shoved back to the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is an edge or margin, such as the grass strip along a road, so a border.

clue.text: Change payment for match official involved with headed ball, say

parts.note: ref is short for referee
to be in something is to be involved with it

indicators.note: headed means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a ball is an example of a dance

explanation.surface: Fees are altered for a referee after a football header incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed ball' suggests a football header; here 'headed' beheads DANCE to leave ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinance a loan is to rearrange how it is paid for, altering the payment terms.

clue.text: Edited alert about help withdrawn in former king's time

indicators.note: about means the word for alert goes around the other piece

parts.note: to alert someone is to warn them

indicators.note: withdrawn here means the word for help is drawn back, read in reverse

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A warning has been edited after support for it was pulled during an old king's reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like it describes the help being cancelled, but it simply turns the word for help around.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the period when Edward VII reigned, 1901 to 1910.

clue.text: Wife: the woman outflanking new, original one at any time

indicators.note: to outflank is to go around the sides, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: her refers to a woman
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A wife, her rival, a newcomer and the first woman of all are lined up together.
explanation.definitionFit: Whenever means at whatever time, on any occasion at all.

clue.text: Shifty eyes'll fit characteristic habits

indicators.note: shifty suggests things moving around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written

explanation.surface: Darting glances will suit someone's typical behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is the typical way a person lives, their usual pattern of behaviour.

clue.text: Pretty woman responsible for break-up?

definitions.meaning: a slang British term for an attractive person
something that smashes things breaks them up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a stunner and literally one who breaks things to pieces.

clue.text: How to make join in stringed instrument

parts.note: banning the letters JO from the word join leaves the word in, which is how to make one into the other

explanation.surface: Instructions for a stringed instrument to join in with the band.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BAN JO: banning JO from JOIN leaves IN, so it is how to turn JOIN into IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a plucked instrument with strings over a drum-like body.

clue.text: Onslaught that could spark pub fight?

definitions.meaning: a heavy concentrated attack or bombardment
fury in a pub, read as ..., could start a brawl

explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a sustained bombardment, and read as bar rage it is anger in a pub.

clue.text: Better to break with infernal nonconformist

indicators.note: breaking things apart scatters their letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An outsider is advised to make a clean break from something hellish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is a person whose unorthodox behaviour shocks the establishment, a maverick.

clue.text: God with name causing sharp irritation

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity with a reputation that annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in the side is a persistent source of annoyance, and a thorn is literally sharp.

clue.text: Pale and black bits evenly distributed in meringue

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the evenly placed bits are the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A light, sugary dessert is spread with dark pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale fawn shade, a light brownish colour.

clue.text: Try last of cases relating to stolen goods

indicators.note: the final letter of the word cases is taken

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen, as in hot goods

explanation.surface: Police make an attempt on the last of their investigations into stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to try it, an attempt.

clue.text: Bend over hot meal, skipping starter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the meal's word loses its first letter, its starter

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone stoops over a hot dish but doesn't bother with the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course; here it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunch is to arch or bend one's back forward, so bending over.

clue.text: To choose, I have to include age for worker

indicators.note: to include means to take within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: to opt is to choose
an era is an age
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a job must take their age into account as a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially one in a factory or a secret agent.

clue.text: Herb stewed in very little open water?

indicators.note: in means the rearranged piece is placed inside the word for very little

parts.note: tiny means very little

indicators.note: stewed suggests ingredients cooked and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook stews a tiny quantity of herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a cooking ingredient but is the fodder that 'stewed' scrambles. The briny is an informal term for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The briny is a jocular name for the sea, the salty open water.

clue.text: Church congregated around new material for bonding

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: around means the word for congregated goes about the other piece

parts.note: people who congregated met

explanation.surface: Churchgoers gathered around new adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is a binding substance used to join bricks, so a material for bonding.
